headline: Senior Software Engineer | Full-Stack & Cloud Systems (React, Node.js, AWS) | Technical Leadership | Growing Focus on AI/LLM Engineering
summary:
I'm a Senior Software Engineer with 6+ years of experience building and running high-traffic web platforms. For the last 4+ years I've been embedded on Dow Jones's Barron's and MarketWatch engineering team, first through Infosys and now with Wizeline, where I lead our 7-engineer team on the account.

My day-to-day covers the full stack of a large publishing platform: Next.js and React on the front end, Node.js and GraphQL services behind it, and the AWS edge in front of everything (CloudFront, Lambda@Edge, WAF, all managed with Terraform). Production incidents are part of the job too. Right now I'm leading the migration of both sites to Next.js App Router and Dow Jones's Index Design System, and I built the AI-assisted tooling the team uses for it.

On the AI side, I designed the infrastructure and backend integration for Barron's AI Stock Screener: Aurora, DynamoDB and private Bedrock endpoints provisioned with Terraform, plus a Python/FastAPI/LangChain multi-agent service running Claude on AWS Bedrock. This is where I want to keep growing: LLM systems, agents, and the infrastructure that makes them reliable in production.

I grew Wizeline's team on this account from one engineer (me) to seven. Along the way I've run around 60 technical interviews across both employers and onboarded every new hire. I also built the sprint metrics tooling that helped the team go from about 80% to 95-100%+ of planned work delivered per sprint; our delivery manager now uses its reports with the client.

I started out in mechanical engineering. My first real program was a VBA macro that cut a two-hour HVAC calculation down to 15 minutes, and I've been automating things and turning them into team tools ever since.

I'm looking for Staff or Tech Lead roles where technical strategy and making the team better count as much as writing code.

description.intro: Tech lead for Wizeline's engineering team embedded in Dow Jones's Barron's & MarketWatch (BMW) group, covering full-stack development, AWS edge infrastructure and production support for both properties.
bullets: Lead the migration of Barron's and MarketWatch from Next.js Pages Router to Next.js 16 App Router and Dow Jones's Index Design System; designed and built the AI-guided migration tool (Claude-based agents, skills and guard hooks with phase-gated plans and immutable baselines) the team uses to move pages and components into the new monorepo.

Architected Barron's AI Stock Screener after inheriting an unrunnable prototype from another team: defined and built its Terraform infrastructure (Aurora MySQL cluster, DynamoDB conversation store, private VPC endpoints to Amazon Bedrock, IAM) inside our multi-account landing zone, and adapted the Python/FastAPI/LangChain multi-agent backend (natural-language-to-SQL over market data, Claude on Bedrock, Langfuse tracing) to run on Barron's platform. #2 contributor on both repos; in coordination with Dow Jones's infrastructure team. Currently in stakeholder evaluation and data-licensing review ahead of launch.

Grew Wizeline's footprint on the account from a single engineer (me) to 7, soon 9: ran ~30 technical interviews (~6 candidates per hire) and onboarded every Wizeline engineer plus Dow Jones direct hires.

Built the sprint-metrics tooling that surfaced under-delivery and blockers; the team went from ~80% to 95-102% of planned work delivered, and its reports are now used by Wizeline's delivery manager in client reporting.

Ran coaching sessions with the client's engineering manager to resolve team-wide performance concerns; act as the technical reference for the client's team lead and Wizeline's delivery manager, unblocking engineers on complex issues.
Respond to production incidents, including hot-fixing regressions mid-deployment on high-traffic pages.
